modules.name: SharedTypes
owns: AuditAction enum (created | updated | deleted | approved | rejected | cancelled)

recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Shared types + AuditLog foundation
recommended_phases.rationale: SharedTypes (LeaveType, LeaveStatus, AuditAction enums) and AuditLog module have zero domain dependencies. AuditLog is required by GP-002 for every state-changing operation downstream. Build these first so every subsequent phase can emit audit records.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: LeavePolicy + Notification
recommended_phases.rationale: LeavePolicy depends only on SharedTypes. Notification depends only on SharedTypes. Both are consumed by later phases but have no cross-dependencies on each other. Can be built in parallel.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: LeaveBalance
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveBalance depends on SharedTypes and LeavePolicy (to know max days per type when initializing). It is a prerequisite for LeaveRequest's submit/approve/reject/cancel flows which must deduct/restore balances.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: LeaveRequest (service + controller + routes)
recommended_phases.rationale: LeaveRequest orchestrates all other modules: validates against LeavePolicy, deducts/restores via LeaveBalance, writes AuditLog records, and fires Notifications. It also exposes the REST API surface. This is the largest and most complex phase.

app_notes: Layer boundaries: Presentation (routes + controllers in LeaveRequest module), Application (all service interfaces + implementations), Domain (models: LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance, LeavePolicy, AuditRecord), Infrastructure (repository implementations, PostgreSQL via Knex, db connection from src/shared/db/connection.ts). Dependencies flow inward: routes → controller → service → repository → db. LeaveRequest is the sole API-surface module; all other modules are internal domain/infrastructure services consumed by LeaveRequest. The Notification module is a fire-and-forget side effect — its failure must not roll back the primary operation. AuditLog writes are synchronous within the transaction boundary per GP-002.

open_questions.question: How is leave balance computed — simple remaining = allocated - used, or does it involve accrual rules (e.g. pro-rata monthly accrual, carry-over from prior year)?
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveBalance.deductBalance, LeaveBalance.initializeBalance, and LeaveRequest.submit validation logic. If accrual-based, the balance module needs a scheduler and a more complex calculation model.
candidate_options: Simple: balance = policy.maxDaysPerYear - sum of approved leave days in fiscal year
Accrual: balance grows monthly/quarterly per policy rules, with carry-over caps

open_questions.question: How is an employee's manager resolved? The LeaveRequest service needs a managerId for routing approvals and notifications.
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveRequest.submit (who to route to), LeaveRequest.getPendingForManager, and Notification.notifyLeaveSubmitted. Without an employee module, the manager lookup contract is undefined.
candidate_options: Employee module exposes IEmployeeService.getManager(employeeId) — LeaveRequest depends on it
ManagerId is passed explicitly by the caller (frontend resolves it)
ManagerId is stored as a claim in the JWT and extracted from request.user

auth_contract: Authenticated request shape: request.user = { id: string; role: UserRole }. UserRole = 'employee' | 'manager' | 'hr_admin'. Identity obtained via JWT bearer token verified by an auth middleware (verifyJwt) that populates request.user. RBAC enforced by a requireRole(...) route-level guard, never inline. Endpoint access: POST /leave-requests → employee; PATCH /leave-requests/:id/approve, PATCH /leave-requests/:id/reject → manager; GET /leave-requests/pending → manager; GET /leave-requests/team-calendar → manager; GET /leave-requests, GET /leave-requests/:id, DELETE /leave-requests/:id → employee (own) or manager (team); GET /leave-balances, POST /leave-policies → hr_admin.
error_response_contract: Standard error shape: { error: string; code: string; details?: unknown }. Validation failure (e.g. endDate before startDate, missing reason) → HTTP 400 { error: "...", code: "VALIDATION_ERROR" }. Authentication failure (missing/invalid JWT) → 401 { error: "Unauthorized", code: "AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED" }. Authorization failure (wrong role) → 403 { error: "Forbidden", code: "INSUFFICIENT_ROLE" }. Not found (unknown requestId) → 404 { error: "Leave request not found", code: "NOT_FOUND" }. Business rule violation (insufficient balance, overlapping dates, policy max exceeded) → 409 { error: "...", code: "BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION" }.
